reads.AORT: mixed — a real flagship-line guidance cut and recall overhang against intact absolute-EBITDA growth, a rising forward path, and a lopsided-bullish sell-side.
reads.BRBR: mixed — a real margin/EBITDA halving into 4.3x leverage, but an intact growing-volume franchise with a dated FY2027 pricing lever.
reads.CNXC: mixed — cash-generative and mix-shifting with rising absolute EBITDA, but a $1.5B impairment, 4.1x leverage and -43% GAAP-EPS cuts keep the terminal case live.
reads.EPAM: mixed — net-cash, still-growing absolute EBITDA and an AI engine offset a management-acknowledged North America growth gap and uniformly negative revenue revisions.
reads.FUBO: mixed — scaled revenue and a contractual EBITDA step-up sit against deep cash burn, a zero-crossing earnings path, and opaque runway.
reads.IT: mixed — a franchise trading at a trough multiple with intact retention/returns but genuinely stalled growth and still-falling estimates.
reads.MVST: strongly-bearish — a stated going-concern doubt plus a ~$104M near-term maturity wall and reversing volume outweigh the FY25 margin inflection.
reads.NCNO: mixed — a genuine positive-EBITDA inflection with below-peer forward multiples, offset by sub-peer decelerating revenue and negative near-term revision breadth.
reads.NFLX: mixed — a real, self-funded compounder (EBITDA/ROIC rising) still on a premium multiple, offset by a ~37% de-rating, negative revenue-revision breadth and peer-lagging EBITDA growth.
reads.SMPL: mixed — a self-funding balance sheet and Quest/pricing levers offset a still-contracting Atkins/OWYN base and downward estimate path.
reads.UBER: strongly-bullish — absolute EBITDA, ROIC and gross-bookings all inflecting up while the multiple sits at its own-history floor.
reads.V: mixed — durable double-digit compounding and a rising-return runway, but the quality is largely paid for at ~21.6x with negative EPS revision breadth.
reads.VITL: mixed — a fortress balance sheet and intact loyal base offset a ~97% forward-EBITDA collapse, cash burn, and still-falling estimates.
reads.VRRM: strongly-bearish — a permanent >10%-of-revenue customer loss plus repeated guidance cuts and a segment impairment outweigh a growing but smaller Government book.
